title: DNS Concepts Practice: Expert Triage
subject: DNS
description: Everyday DNS incidents using evidence-first triage → diagnosis → fix. Titles and summaries are symptom-based to keep root cause discovery inside the workflow.
reportOverview: This report summarizes ticket outcomes and change notes for DNS concepts practice. Use it to review your evidence interpretation and troubleshooting path.
evidenceInstructions:
Instructions:
1) Read the symptom and review the evidence.
2) Choose the first thing you would verify (Triage).
3) Pick the most likely cause based on the evidence (Diagnosis).
4) Select the best remediation step (Fix).
5) Write a short change note describing what changed and how you validated it.

tickets.title: Workstation: 'The specified domain does not exist'
tickets.summary: A newly imaged workstation fails to join the domain. Internet access works, but the domain join wizard reports it cannot locate a domain controller.
validations: Confirm client is using internal DNS (DCs).
Confirm SRV lookup resolves after change.
tickets.debrief: Active Directory relies on SRV (Service) records to help clients find Domain Controllers. Public DNS resolvers (8.8.8.8) cannot see your internal SRV records, which is why the join failed despite having internet access.

triage.q: The client has internet access but cannot find the Domain. What is the most effective investigative command to run first?
options: ipconfig /all to check which DNS resolvers are currently assigned to the NIC
ping -t <Domain_Name> to check for basic connectivity
systeminfo to see the current build number
net accounts to check for password policy conflicts

diagnosis.q: The evidence shows NXDOMAIN for the SRV record and DNS servers pointing to Google (8.8.8.8). Why is the join failing?
options: The Domain Controller is powered off
Public DNS servers lack the internal SRV records needed for Active Directory location services
The workstation's firewall is blocking LDAP traffic
The workstation is using an invalid IP address

fix.q: What is the best permanent remediation?
options: Add the DC's IP to the local 'hosts' file
Update the DHCP Scope Option 006 to point clients to the internal DNS servers (DCs)
Run 'ipconfig /flushdns' three times
Re-image the workstation with a different OS version

tickets.title: Post-Migration: Stale Site Content
tickets.summary: After an intranet migration (10.0.10.15 -> 10.0.20.25), most users reach the new server. However, five users in accounting still see the old site.
validations: Verify client cache clears and shows new record.
nslookup returns new IP on affected client.
tickets.debrief: This is a classic 'TTL (Time to Live)' issue. Even if the server is updated, clients keep the old IP in their local cache until the TTL expires. Flushing the cache manually overrides this timer.

triage.q: The server is updated, but some clients still see the old IP. Where should you look for the discrepancy?
options: The DNS Server's Forwarders list
The client's local DNS resolver cache using 'ipconfig /displaydns'
The Active Directory Sites and Services console
The IIS configuration on the new server

diagnosis.q: Based on the TTL of 290 remaining in the artifact, what is the root cause?
options: The DNS server has not yet replicated to other Domain Controllers
The client is holding a valid, unexpired copy of the old record in its local memory
The new intranet server is not responding to ICMP pings
The accounting VLAN is being blocked by a firewall

fix.q: How do you resolve this for the affected users immediately?
options: Reboot the DNS server
Run 'ipconfig /flushdns' on the affected clients
Delete the record from DNS and wait 24 hours
Change the client's subnet mask

tickets.title: Organization-Wide External Outage
tickets.summary: Internal names resolve perfectly, but all external websites (Google, Microsoft) stopped resolving immediately after a junior admin made a 'cleanup' change.
artifact: DNS Console: A new zone named '.' (a single dot) appears in Forward Lookup Zones.
validations: Confirm external lookups succeed after fix.
Confirm internal zones continue to resolve.
tickets.debrief: By creating a root '.' zone, the admin told the server that it is the authority for the entire internet. The server stopped using forwarders or root hints because it thought it already had all the answers (despite having no records).

triage.q: Internal resolution is healthy, but external is dead. What visual indicator in the DNS Manager console explains why recursion is failing?
options: The presence of a Root Zone (the '.' zone) in Forward Lookup Zones
The 'Forwarders' tab is greyed out
The server icon has a yellow exclamation mark
The Reverse Lookup zone is missing

diagnosis.q: Why does a '.' zone break external resolution?
options: It encrypts all outgoing UDP traffic
It forces the server to believe it is the 'Root' of the entire DNS hierarchy, disabling recursion to the actual internet
It causes a IP conflict with the gateway
It marks the server as 'Unauthorized' in Active Directory

fix.q: What is the fastest way to restore internet resolution?
options: Reinstall the DNS Role
Delete the '.' (root) zone and ensure Forwarders/Root Hints are active
Add google.com as a CNAME in the internal zone
Disable the Windows Firewall on the DC
